summary.summary: Bexley ended 2025/26 with £249.6m of debt (£224.6m long-dated PWLB at 3.34% plus £25m of short-term loans from other councils at an average 5.97%) against just £10.1m of investments, after cash balances more than halved in the year from £21.6m. The £25m of temporary borrowing was taken in February-March 2026 purely to keep the council liquid, at rates up to 7%, and all of it falls due in April 2026. The CFR outturn was £318.6m against £249.6m of borrowing, and the CIPFA liability benchmark shows existing loans are insufficient to meet the projected CFR, so more long-term borrowing is coming. All prudential limits were met and no limit was exceeded on any day.

news_drafts.headline: Bexley eligible for grant covering 90% of its schools high needs deficit, subject to government approval of its SEND plan
news_drafts.lead:
Bexley would receive a grant covering 90% of its accumulated deficit on funding for children with special educational needs, if the government approves its reform plan. The borough's Schools Forum was told the council is eligible for a High Needs Stability Grant, payable in autumn 2026.

The deficit sits in the high needs part of the dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools. High needs is the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The papers put the grant at 90% of the accumulated high needs deficit as at 31 March 2026. They do not give the deficit in pounds, and the grant is conditional: the council's paper says it is "subject to approval of the plan".

The plan is Bexley's Local SEND Reform Plan, which the council submitted to the Department for Education (DfE) on 19 June 2026. Decisions on plans were expected in September 2026. The paper presented to the forum describes the grant as resolving a material accumulated deficit in the high needs block.

The papers do not say whether the plan has yet been approved.

findings.headline: Maintained schools sector is shrinking through ongoing academisation, eroding the baseline of per-pupil contribution income
findings.detail: The council applies a 2027-28 budget reduction to account for 2026-27 academisations. Per-pupil contributions are rising 2% (from £26.62 to £27.15 for mainstream pupils; £131.35 to £133.98 for special places), but total contribution income falls from £159k to £153k because the maintained school pupil base is contracting as schools convert to academy status.
findings.matters: Finance directors need to track the ongoing erosion of maintained schools funding bases as academisation continues; this is structural demand loss that affects local authority income
findings.figures: Maintained sector total contribution: £159k (2026-27) → £153k (2027-28); per-pupil charge increases: £26.62 → £27.15 mainstream, £131.35 → £133.98 special places
findings.quote: For 2027-28 a reduction to the budgets has been applied to account for the 26-27 academisation, and a 3% inflation uplift has been applied to take account of the local government pay award.

findings.headline: Bexley is absorbing the £36k historic commitments cut through staff savings and increasing High Needs transfers
findings.detail: The council states it has responded to funding cuts through staff savings and transferring costs to the High Needs Block. For 2027-28, it proposes increasing the High Needs transfer by £17k, which will partially offset the £36k reduction in historic commitments funding expected that year. The remaining £19k gap is addressed through staff reductions and cost transfers.
findings.matters: Shows how councils are managing structural DfE cuts by rebalancing internal allocations and accepting staff reductions, a pattern others may need to follow
findings.figures: Historic commitments reduction: £36k; proposed High Needs transfer increase: £17k; gap to be closed by staff savings and transfers: £19k
findings.quote: The Council has responded through a combination of staff savings and transferring costs to the High Needs Block where possible, as noted at f) above.

findings.headline: DfE historic commitments funding for early intervention is being cut 20% annually, from £868k to an estimated £146k by 2027-28
findings.detail: Schools Forum committed to £868k for early intervention services in 2015, which the DfE initially funded as historic commitments. From 2020-21, the DfE began cutting this by 20% annually. By 2027-28, if this pattern continues, the allocation will fall to £146k. This is a structural, ongoing reduction with no replenishment, leaving the council to manage a shrinking funding base.
findings.matters: Other councils managing DSG will face this same systematic cuts from the DfE and need to see how peers are responding to an erosion of historic commitments that shows no signs of stopping
findings.quote: Since 2020-21 the DfE has reduced this historic commitments funding by 20% each year. If this pattern continues in 2027/28 funding will reduce from £182kto £146k.

findings.headline: Bexley has received £2.137m in Experts at Hand funding for 2026/27, with potential larger allocations in future years if it maintains its 0.498% share of national funding.
findings.detail: From the national £429m Experts at Hand and SEND Transformation fund, Bexley's allocation for 2026/27 is £2.137m. The paper projects that if the national fund reaches £750m (2027/28) and £850m (2028/29) and Bexley retains its 0.498% share, future allocations could reach £3.735m and £4.233m respectively. Spending is restricted by DfE guidance to specific professional roles and transformation activities.
findings.matters: This is new recurring revenue with significant multi-year potential. Other councils and lenders need to understand how SEND reform funding flows to local areas and what constraints apply, particularly given the strict restrictions on eligible spending.
findings.figures: £2.137m 2026/27; projected £3.735m 2027/28 and £4.233m 2028/29 (if Bexley's allocation percentage holds); national fund £429m
findings.quote: For 2026/27 the Government has committed £429m Experts at Hand & Local Authority SEND Transformation funding nationally, of which Bexley has received £2.137m.

findings.headline: Bexley is eligible for a High Needs Stability Grant addressing 90% of its accumulated Dedicated Schools Grant High Needs deficit.
findings.detail: Subject to plan approval, Bexley will receive the grant in Autumn 2026. The reform plan was submitted to the DfE on 19 June 2026 with decisions expected in September 2026. This grant resolves a material accumulated deficit in the High Needs Block.
findings.matters: Finance directors at Bexley and peers managing similar pressures need to understand how significant accumulated deficits are being resolved. The grant scheme terms and its conditional nature are material to assessing the council's financial position.
findings.figures: 90% of accumulated DSG High Needs deficit as at 31 March 2026
findings.quote: Subject to approval of the plan, Bexley would be eligible to receive a High Needs Stability Grant, payable in Autumn 2026, which would address 90% of the accumulated Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) High Needs deficit as at 31 March 2026.
